title: Company Handbook: Working at Redwood — Roles, Benefits, Hiring & Tools
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This page is the canonical high-level handbook entry for working at Redwood. It summarizes how we work, role and career ladder expectations, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding experience, and the primary internal tools new and existing employees rely on. Use this page as a landing point; the Related Resources section links into more detailed guides and policies.

1) Working at Redwood

Intro: Redwood is a developer-first, production-inference company. We are mission-driven and expect high craftsmanship, pragmatic trade-offs, and clear communication. Our working model balances focus time and collaboration for distributed teams.

Key principles:
- Mission-first: prioritize customer-facing reliability and performance improvements.
- Respectful, data-informed decisions: use evidence (benchmarks, telemetry, customer signals) when evaluating tradeoffs.
- Ownership: engineers and PMs take end-to-end responsibility for features and services.
- Inclusion & growth: support diverse perspectives and individual learning.

Work model:
- Remote-first with regional hubs (San Francisco, New York, London).
- Core collaboration hours: 10:00–15:00 local team time recommended for synchronous meetings.
- Asynchronous-first for design docs, RFCs, and decision records.
- Travel and in-person events: quarterly team offsites and annual company summit.

Communication expectations:
- All long-form proposals should be posted to Confluence and linked in PRs.
- Use Slack for signals and short discussions; escalate incidents via PagerDuty and the incident channel.

2) Roles and Career Ladders

High-level structure: Redwood maintains two career tracks: Individual Contributor (IC) and Manager. Each track has levels using our internal leveling framework (IC-1 through IC-6; MGR-1 through MGR-4). Level expectations are summarized below; full leveling rubrics live in the Roles and Onboarding guide.

IC path (summary):
- IC-1 (Junior Engineer / Associate): learns the codebase, delivers small features with guidance.
- IC-2 (Engineer): owns small services, reliable delivery of scoped work.
- IC-3 (Senior Engineer): leads medium-sized projects, mentors juniors, influences design.
- IC-4 (Staff Engineer): drives cross-team technical initiatives, defines APIs/standards.
- IC-5 (Senior Staff / Principal): shapes product and platform strategy, owns broad system integrity.
- IC-6 (Distinguished / Architect): company-level technical leadership (rare).

Manager path (summary):
- MGR-1 (First-time Manager): manages 1–3 individual contributors, focuses on career growth and team delivery.
- MGR-2: manages multiple teams or a larger product area.
- MGR-3+: senior leadership roles (Director/Head).

Promotion criteria (common signals):
- Consistent delivery of scope with high quality and measurable impact.
- Evidence of leadership beyond current level: cross-team influence, mentoring, owning critical incidents or initiatives.
- Product and customer awareness: ability to balance technical trade-offs with business and cost considerations.
- Clear examples in the promotion packet: design docs, measurable outcomes, peer feedback.

Promotion process (high level):
1. Candidate prepares promotion packet (self-assessment, 3–5 impact examples, PRs/designs).
2. Manager and peer reviewers provide written feedback.
3. Calibration panel reviews packet and provides decision (level up / retain / development plan).
4. HR coordinates the outcome and updates compensation as appropriate.

Leveling owners: People Ops maintains rubrics; engineering managers and the Director of People Ops are owners for calibration.

3) Benefits and Perks

Summary: Redwood offers competitive total compensation (salary + equity + cash bonuses when applicable) and a benefits package designed for distributed teams. This section summarizes common items; full plan documents and enrollment steps are in Benefits & Perks (HR portal).

Compensation:
- Market-competitive base salary with regionally adjusted bands.
- Equity grants on hire (standard option RSU plan) and refresh cycles for sustained high performers.
- Annual performance review and budgeted merit increases.

Healthcare & wellness:
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer subsidy (US/UK/EU plans supported).
- Flexible Spending Account (FSA) / Health Savings Account (HSA) where applicable.
- Mental health and EAP benefits; wellness stipend: $200/year.

Time off & leave:
- Flexible PTO policy (manager-approved) with recommended minimum of 15 days off per year.
- Parental leave: primary caregiver 18 weeks paid (US policy), secondary caregiver 8 weeks paid; regional variations apply.
- Public holidays and company-wide shutdown (usually week between Christmas and New Year).

Learning & development:
- Education stipend: $1,200/year for books, courses, conferences.
- Conference & travel budget for approved technical events.
- Internal learning hours: 0.25 FTE allocation for career growth (team-managed).

Additional perks:
- Home office stipend on hire ($500) and refresh on role change.
- Commuter benefits where applicable.
- Quarterly team celebration budget.
- Early access to Redwood products and credits for Dedicated/Private testing.

4) Hiring and Onboarding Overview

Hiring philosophy: hire for mission fit, technical craft, curiosity, and ability to operate in a production-first engineering culture. Our interview loop emphasizes system design, practical coding, and collaboration (pairing).

Standard interview loop (software engineering):
1. Recruiter screen (30 min): role fit, compensation expectations, logistics.
2. Technical screen (45–60 min): coding or system-design focused pairing exercise.
3. Onsite / virtual loop (3–5 interviews):
   - System design (scalable inference, runtime reliability, infra cost control)
   - Coding (practical coding tasks, debugging)
   - Behavioral / collaboration (communication, ownership)
   - Culture and mission fit (values and equity mindset)
4. Hiring Committee review and offer decision.

Offer & negotiation: Comp packages are handled by People Ops; negotiation guidance balances internal equity and market alignment. Recruiters should use the published compensation bands.

New hire onboarding (first 90 days):
- Day 0–1: paperwork, equipment provisioning, account access (Okta SSO, GitHub, Slack, Confluence).
- Week 1: orientation (company overview, security brief), team onboarding sessions, meet your buddy and manager.
- Month 1: ship a small task, setup dev environment, attend cross-team onboarding.
- Month 2: take ownership of a feature or service, begin to own on-call rotations if applicable.
- Month 3: present a 30/60/90 progress review with manager, set growth goals and potential impact projects.

New hire checklist (short):
- Complete HR forms and benefits enrollment.
- Confirm laptop and SSH access; verify VPN and KMS access for private deployments if required.
- Join team Slack channels, subscribe to weekly engineering digest, and complete security training.

Buddy program: each new hire is assigned a buddy for the first 90 days — a peer-level contact for onboarding questions and cultural orientation.

5) Internal Tools Guide (quick reference)

Primary tools and purpose:
- Okta (SSO): primary identity provider for all company apps.
- GitHub: source control and code reviews (team-owned repos under org redwood-inference).
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions and Argo workflows for deployments; use the dev-deploy pipeline for staging.
- Datadog: metrics, dashboards, and alerting (opens with SSO).
- Sentry: error monitoring and crash reporting.
- Slack: day-to-day communication, incident channels (#incidents, #ops).
- Confluence: internal documentation (this space).
- PagerDuty: on-call routing and escalation.
- HR Portal: benefits enrollment, payroll, PTO requests.
- Redwood Console (internal dev): staging deployments and model catalog preview.

Access & request process:
- Request tool access via the IT Self-Service form (link in HR Portal) or Slack @it-ops.
- Approvals: manager should approve access requests for production-level permissions and KMS keys.

Common CLI snippets and tips:
- Clone the main monorepo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/platform.git
- Start local environment (dev container): make dev-up && make dev-db-seed
- Deploy to dev: gh workflow run dev-deploy.yml --ref=main --repo redwood-inference/platform
- Check logs: datadog logs query "service:runtime AND env:staging" --limit 50

Security notes for tooling:
- Never commit secrets. Use vault.redwood or KMS for secrets in CI.
- SSH keys should be uploaded to Okta-managed GitHub; rotate keys annually.

6) Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Who do I contact for payroll questions?
A: People Ops (payroll@redwood.com) or the HR Portal support ticketing flow.

Q: How do I request sponsor travel or conference budget?
A: Submit a budget request via the internal travel booking page; manager approval is required for conferences.

Q: What is Redwood’s remote work allowance?
A: New hires receive a $500 home office stipend and may be eligible for regional remote work allowances per manager and People Ops approval.

8) Ownership and maintenance

Document owner: People Ops (Maya Patel).
Review cadence: annual review or when policies change (e.g., benefits vendor, parental leave update, major workforce changes).
Change process: submit edits as a Confluence pull request (use the handbook-edit template), notify reviewers, and publish after People Ops sign-off.

If you notice omissions or outdated information, please file a doc update request in the #handbook-updates Slack channel.

Acknowledgements: This handbook page was assembled with input from Eng leadership, People Ops, and Finance.
